extracted.intended_audience: general public and citizens interested in political reform, republican principles, and the theory/practice of government
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts normative criteria and standards Thomas Paine advances for evaluating forms of government, the legitimacy of revolution, and the rights/sources of sovereignty. Emphasizes what makes governments just or corrupt and how nations ought to reform or abolish governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monarchy and aristocracy rest on ignorance (not reason)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Those two distinct and opposite forms erect themselves on the two distinct and opposite bases of Reason and Ignorance.--As the exercise of Government requires talents and abilities, and as talents and abilities cannot have hereditary descent, it is evident that hereditary succession requires a belief from man to which his reason cannot subscribe, and which can only be established upon his ignorance; and the more ignorant any country is, the better it is fitted for this species of Government."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paine argues hereditary succession is incompatible with reason because talents/abilities are not heritable; therefore monarchy/aristocracy rely on beliefs beyond reason and thrive where ignorance is greatest.

rubrics_metrics.name: A well-constituted republic requires only reason
rubrics_metrics.description: "Government, in a well-constituted republic, requires no belief from man beyond what his reason can give. He sees the rationale of the whole system, its origin and its operation; and as it is best supported when best understood, the human faculties act with boldness..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In republics, understanding and reason support the system; broad, comprehensible representation makes governance resilient and encourages civic virtue and bold public engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed governments are necessarily driven by corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: "The moving power in this species of Government is, of necessity, Corruption."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paine contends that mixed governments (combining monarchy, aristocracy, democracy) lack a coherent rational foundation, require buying off elements, and therefore depend on corruption to hold disparate parts together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed governments lack responsibility and evade accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: In mixed Governments "there is no responsibility: the parts cover each other till responsibility is lost; and the corruption which moves the machine, contrives at the same time its own escape... When it is laid down as a maxim, that a King can do no wrong, it places him in a state of similar security... It then descends upon the Minister, who shelters himself under a majority in Parliament..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because roles overlap and actors justify multiple characters, blame is passed around; offices, majorities, and patronage hide wrongdoing and make responsibility diffuse or absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: A mixed government becomes a government by committee (same persons acting in multiple roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mixed Government "finally resolving itself into a Government by Committee; in which the advisers, the actors, the approvers, the justifiers, the persons responsible, and the persons not responsible, are the same persons."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paine warns that theatrical separations of power can conceal a concentration of power in a self‑protecting group that mutually praises and justifies itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: In a republic representation is equal and parts are unified
rubrics_metrics.description: In a well‑constituted republic "the representation being equal throughout the country, and complete in itself... The parts are not foreigners to each other, like democracy, aristocracy, and monarchy. As there are no discordant distinctions, there is nothing to corrupt by compromise... Public measures appeal of themselves to the understanding of the Nation..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equal, comprehensive representation aligns governmental parts with the nation, removing the need for flattering appeals to vanity or corrupt compromises; public policy stands or falls on merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes are legitimate if necessary; apology for taxes implies impeachment
rubrics_metrics.description: "If taxes are necessary, they are of course advantageous; but if they require an apology, the apology itself implies an impeachment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paine asserts that necessary taxes are justified; persistent lamenting or apologizing for taxes indicates misuse or a failing government that should be challenged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government is not the private property of rulers; sovereignty belongs to the nation
rubrics_metrics.description: "What is government more than the management of the affairs of a Nation? It is not, and from its nature cannot be, the property of any particular man or family... Sovereignty, as a matter of right, appertains to the Nation only, and not to any individual; and a Nation has at all times an inherent indefeasible right to abolish any form of Government it finds inconvenient..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legitimacy of government derives from national consent; citizens retain the right to reform or abolish governments that do not serve the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every citizen is a member of the sovereignty and owes obedience only to the laws
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every citizen is a member of the Sovereignty, and, as such, can acknowledge no personal subjection; and his obedience can be only to the laws."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal subjection to rulers is illegitimate; lawful obedience must be to laws created by the sovereign people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government must possess knowledge of what it governs; republican representation supplies that knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: When considering government "they must necessarily suppose it to possess a knowledge of all the objects and matters upon which its authority is to be exercised... the republican system... operates to embrace the whole of a Nation; and the knowledge necessary to the interest of all the parts, is to be found in the center, which the parts by representation form..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective governance requires informed understanding of national interests; representative republican institutions concentrate and make accessible the needed knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revolutions in America and France are a universal renovation based on principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Paine characterizes those revolutions as "a renovation of the natural order of things, a system of principles as universal as truth and the existence of man, and combining moral with political happiness and national prosperity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These revolutions are not mere local events but exemplify principles applicable broadly; they justify rethinking older governmental forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of fundamental political principles (I–III)
rubrics_metrics.description: I. "Men are born, and always continue, free and equal in respect of their rights. Civil distinctions, therefore, can be founded only on public utility." II. "The end of all political associations is the preservation of the natural and imprescriptible rights of man; and these rights are liberty, property, security, and resistance of oppression." III. "The nation is essentially the source of all sovereignty; nor can any Individual, or Any Body Of Men, be entitled to any authority which is not expressly derived from it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paine sets a compact set of foundational standards for just government: natural equality of rights; purpose of political association to secure natural rights (liberty, property, security, resistance to oppression); and popular sovereignty as the only legitimate source of authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monarchical sovereignty is the enemy of mankind and a principal cause of war
rubrics_metrics.description: "Monarchical sovereignty, the enemy of mankind, and the source of misery, is abolished; and the sovereignty itself is restored to its natural and original place, the Nation. Were this the case throughout Europe, the cause of wars would be taken away."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paine links monarchical systems to militarism and perpetual war; restoring sovereignty to peoples would remove incentives for interstate conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: War is profitable to old governments and thus perpetuated
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every war terminates with an addition of taxes, and consequently with an addition of revenue; and in any event of war... the power and interest of Governments are increased. War, therefore, from its productiveness... becomes a principal part of the system of old Governments..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional incentives (taxation, appointments, revenue) incline entrenched governments toward war; proposals to abolish war are resisted because they would remove lucrative branches of government power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republics are less likely to wage war because their interest aligns with the nation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Why are not Republics plunged into war, but because the nature of their Government does not admit of an interest distinct from that of the Nation?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When government officers' interests coincide with the national interest, there is less motive to engage in wars of revenue or aggrandizement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and produce revolutions by reason and accommodation rather than convulsion
rubrics_metrics.description: "As it is not difficult to perceive... that hereditary Governments are verging to their decline, and that Revolutions on the broad basis of national sovereignty and Government by representation, are making their way in Europe, it would be an act of wisdom to anticipate their approach, and produce Revolutions by reason and accommodation, rather than commit them to the issue of convulsions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paine recommends proactive, reasoned reform processes to avoid violent upheaval; where possible, change should be arranged peacefully and rationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigating and criticizing governments is a public right; prosecution for such inquiry is despotism
rubrics_metrics.description: "It would be an act of despotism... to make a law to prohibit investigating the principles, good or bad, on which such a law, or any other is founded... The defects of every government and constitution... must... be as open to discussion as the defects of a law... those subjects... are always before a country as a matter of right, and cannot, without invading the general rights of that country, be made subjects for prosecution."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open public inquiry into principles and constitutions is a civic duty; criminal prosecutions to silence such debate are illegitimate and dangerous to public rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Better to obey a bad law while arguing for its repeal than to break it by force
rubrics_metrics.description: "I have always held it an opinion... that it is better to obey a bad law, making use at the same time of every argument to show its errors and procure its repeal, than forcibly to violate it; because the precedent of breaking a bad law might weaken the force, and lead to a discretionary violation, of those which are good."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paine endorses lawful, argumentative reform over unlawful resistance to avoid setting harmful precedents for discretionary lawbreaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: National questions are not for a jury of twelve; require a convention of the whole nation
rubrics_metrics.description: "On all cases that apply universally to a nation... a jury of twelve men is not competent to decide... The only effectual jury in such cases would be a convention of the whole nation fairly elected; for in all such cases the whole nation is the vicinage."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters concerning the constitution or fundamental national rights should be resolved by broad, representative assemblies (conventions), not ordinary criminal juries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prejudices from education and habit yield to reason and reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: "As to the prejudices which men have from education and habit, in favour of any particular form or system of government, those prejudices have yet to stand the test of reason and reflection... No man is prejudiced in favour of a thing, knowing it to be wrong. He is attached to it on the belief of its being right; and when he sees it is not so, the prejudice will be gone."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paine claims that informed reasoning can overturn culturally entrenched attachments to unjust political systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Society and civilisation provide order independent of government
rubrics_metrics.description: "Great part of that order which reigns among mankind is not the effect of government. It has its origin in the principles of society and the natural constitution of man. It existed prior to government, and would exist if the formality of government was abolished."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many social goods (order, industry, civilisation) arise from social nature and institutions rather than from government; thus reformers should differentiate effects of government from those of society when arguing for change.
